title: Fear not, little flock (Luke 12:22–34)
hookLine: it's your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom

lines: A SMALL BAND ON A DUSTY ROAD.
cards: This time the words are for his disciples, not the crowd. Fishermen who left their boats. A former tax collector.
Women supporting the group out of their own means. No house of their own, no regular income, heading toward Jerusalem with a teacher who keeps making powerful people angry.
If anyone had reason to lie awake doing sums, it was this group. And he looks at them, a small band on a dusty road, and calls them by a tender name.

teach.b: First he points at the sky: "Consider the ravens: for they neither sow nor reap; which neither have storehouse nor barn; and God feedeth them." Matthew just says the birds.
Luke names ravens, scavengers, a bird the law of Moses listed as unclean. Even the bird nobody would put on a greeting card is fed.
Then the field: "Consider the lilies how they grow: they toil not, they spin not; and yet I say unto you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these."
Then a sharp little question: which of you, by worrying, can add one cubit to your height, or a single hour to your life?
And the line Luke saves for last: "Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom."
Little flock: small, vulnerable, the kind of group a wolf would notice. He doesn't pretend they're strong. He says they're loved.

teach.h: GOOD PLEASURE: GOD DELIGHTS TO GIVE.
teach.b: Good pleasure is a warm phrase in Greek, from the same family as the angels' good will toward men at his birth, and the voice at his baptism: in thee I am well pleased.
In Jesus' words, the kingdom isn't handed over reluctantly, after enough worry. It's the Father's delight to give it.
Then: sell what you have, give alms, keep treasure where moths and thieves can't reach. The giving follows the not fearing.
And the line that sums up the chapter so far: "For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also."

how: Some Christians return to this passage in times of money worry, and some religious communities, such as Franciscan friars and Poor Clares, give up personal possessions as a discipline of trust.

o: don't be afraid; God delights to give
never worry, since nothing bad will happen
a warning to hide from those in power

games.q: what's inside Luke 12:22–34 — tap the pairs.
p: no storehouse, and God feeds them

s: Luke names the ravens, a bird the law of Moses counted unclean
Matthew says the birds of the air; Luke says ravens. even the scavenger is fed.
Jesus says Solomon in his glory outshone the lilies
"Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these."
the kingdom is given reluctantly, after enough effort
"it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom." good pleasure means delight.

games.q: you're one of a small band of disciples with no income and no home, walking toward trouble. what does Jesus call you?
games.why: "fear not, little flock; for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom." he doesn't call them strong. he calls them loved.

practice: Let one worry about money or the future come up and name it plainly, then think of the ravens, fed without a barn, and let it sit a little lighter.

Think of one thing you could give away, a coat you don't wear, a book you've finished, something you'd notice but not miss terribly, and picture handing it over. If you pray, say the line quietly: fed without a barn.

wordCard.voice: Fear not. Jesus' words to a small, vulnerable band of followers: it is your Father's good pleasure, God's delight, to give you the kingdom.

orig.note: Greek: was pleased, took delight. Luke uses the same word family for good will at the birth and for well pleased at the baptism.

carryVoice: Your line: fed without a barn. Ravens keep no storehouse, and they're fed. That's day five hundred forty-nine.
